# Know why each step matters

no-vibe now tells you why you are doing each step, not only what its goal is, so you can see how today's exercise leads to what you want to build.

## What changed

- A reason for every step. Before each chapter, section and exercise, the agent says why it is needed and how it leads to the goal above it: an exercise to its section goal, a section to its chapter goal, a chapter to your book goal.
- Concrete reasons. The agent names what you could not do without the step, and gives a new reason each time.
- Plans still adapt. The agent says where a step leads, not what the next section will be, because it still plans each section from how you are doing.
- Everything stays in scope. If the agent cannot link a section or exercise to the goal, it replaces it with one it can link. It asks you before skipping a chapter.
- Build chapters and resume. Build sections say why they are needed, and when you resume a lesson the agent says why the current section matters for the goal.

## Upgrade

- Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace update no-vibe`, then restart.
- Codex: `codex plugin marketplace upgrade no-vibe`, then remove and add the plugin again.
- Pi: `pi install npm:no-vibe` once 3.3.0 is on npm, or `pi install git:github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- Antigravity: `agy plugin install https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- opencode: `opencode reload`.

Full changes: https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe/compare/v3.2.0...v3.3.0

# Clearer explanations

no-vibe now defines how the agent explains, so you can follow a lesson and remember what matters from it. Your choice of how you like to learn still applies.

## What changed

- What to remember. The agent works out the 1 to 3 things from a section you should remember and says them up front.
- Terms first. The agent explains a term in plain words before using it, unless you already know it.
- Break it down, put it back together. The agent explains an idea in small pieces, then joins them into one complete, structured explanation.
- Code explained properly. Code tied to the section or chapter goal is explained as the big picture, then the core, then how it works, not a one-sentence summary. Complex code is split into parts inside the same section. Other code only gets a brief mention.
- Small sections stay short. A section such as one piece of syntax gets a short plain explanation and skips the code walkthrough.
- No length limit. The limit of about 5 sentences per turn is gone, and the agent takes the space an explanation needs. This is an experiment, so feedback on message length is welcome.

## Upgrade

- Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace update no-vibe`, then restart.
- Codex: `codex plugin marketplace upgrade no-vibe`, then remove and add the plugin again.
- Pi: `pi install npm:no-vibe` once 3.2.0 is on npm, or `pi install git:github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- Antigravity: `agy plugin install https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- opencode: `opencode reload`.

Full changes: https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe/compare/v3.1.0...v3.2.0

# Lessons as a book

no-vibe now teaches a lesson like a book: chapters that build on each other toward your goal, sections planned on the fly from how you are doing, and a check at the end of every chapter.

## What changed

- Chapters and sections. The syllabus you approve lists chapters, each with a title and the goal you reach by its end. Inside a chapter the agent plans one section at a time, tells you its goal before teaching, and gives at least 3 exercises with the full code for you to type. From how you do, it picks the next section: more practice, another explanation, or the next step.
- Chapter check. Each chapter ends with tasks on its core ideas, such as finding a bug, predicting output or fixing broken code. The agent explains what you miss again until you get it, then asks whether anything is still unclear.
- Build chapters. A goal can be building something in your own project. After the foundation chapters, the agent reads the code the feature touches, reuses what exists, follows the project's style, and shows each piece for you to type into your own files.
- Practice folder. The agent asks once where you want to practice: `.no-vibe/practice/` in an existing project, or the current folder otherwise.
- Answer in your own words. Every multiple-choice question ends with an open option worded for that question.
- Notes. `.no-vibe/syllabus.md` keeps the agent's notes on each section and uses them when you resume.
- New header: `[no-vibe] Step: <context|level|goal|syllabus|learn|exercise|check> · Chapter: <n/total|-> · Section: <k|-> · Exercise: <k|->`. The resume line now reads `(chapter n/total)`. Syllabus files from 3.0.0 still resume.
- A shorter README.

## Upgrade

- Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace update no-vibe`, then restart.
- Codex: `codex plugin marketplace upgrade no-vibe`, then remove and add the plugin again.
- Pi: `pi install npm:no-vibe` once 3.1.0 is on npm, or `pi install git:github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- Antigravity: `agy plugin install https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`.
- opencode: `opencode reload`.

Full changes: https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe/compare/v3.0.0...v3.1.0

# A simpler teaching flow that fits your project

no-vibe now teaches in five short steps, reads your existing project before asking anything, and builds every runtime from one source.

## Breaking changes

- Gemini CLI support is removed. The supported runtimes are Claude Code, Codex, opencode, Pi and Antigravity.
- The teaching flow and its state changed. A lesson now lives in `.no-vibe/syllabus.md`, and older state files are not read.
- opencode support targets the v2 plugin API.

## What changed

- Five steps per lesson. Level is found with concrete multiple-choice questions, the goal is agreed until it fits one sentence, the syllabus starts as a draft you approve, each section has a short lesson (concept first or code first), and each section has at least 3 exercises with the full code shown so you build muscle memory by typing it. Later sections reuse earlier material.
- Project context. In an existing project the agent first reads it and saves a summary to `.no-vibe/project.md`: stack and versions, structure, conventions, what works and what is open. Level questions, goal options and the syllabus then fit the project, and nothing it teaches asks you to rewrite what already works. Exercises stay standalone practice in the same stack. With no project, this step is skipped.
- One source of truth. A generator writes every per-runtime file from `no-vibe.config.json` and the skills, and `npm run check` fails when a generated file is stale.
- One write guard. Shared shell hooks with no `jq` or `realpath` dependency, used by every runtime. The Bash guard is best-effort, and the README lists what it does not catch.

## Install

Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add rizukirr/no-vibe
/plugin install no-vibe@no-vibe
```

Codex:

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add rizukirr/no-vibe
codex plugin add no-vibe --marketplace no-vibe
```

Pi: `pi install npm:no-vibe`

Antigravity: `agy plugin install https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe`

opencode: see the README.

Full changes: https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe/compare/v2.0.3...v3.0.0

# Codex marketplace, npm publish prep, disclosure modes

First stable release covering the **disclosure-mode redesign** (started in v2.0.3-beta01) and **distribution reach** to the Codex plugin marketplace and the npm registry.

## Highlights

- **Codex marketplace install.** `codex plugin install no-vibe` now works end-to-end. Codex moves from instruction-only soft-block to a real hard-block on `apply_patch` and shell write attempts — the existing Claude hook scripts are reused via Codex's `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` / legacy `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`.
- **Disclosure modes (guided write vs. showcase).** Guided write is now the default Phase 3 path: AI walks the user toward the code in English with graded help verbs (`hint` / `analogy` / `pseudo` / `show` / `less`) so the code the user types comes from a decision they made, not from transcribing a block. Showcase remains available as a fallback.
- **Prediction gate.** Every Phase 3 layer now ends with a one-question prediction targeting an edge case, intermediate value, branch, or failure mode — never a value already named in the expected-output signature. The run becomes a self-test rather than passive verification.
- **Anti-sycophancy and locator-anchored critique.** Phase 4 review now resists agreement spirals on user rebuttals and ties every critique line to a precise locator in the user's code.
- **First-class native install per CLI in the README.** Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Gemini CLI, OpenCode — each now has a one-step install snippet using its native CLI command.
- **npm-publish ready.** `LICENSE` (MIT), full `package.json` metadata (`license`, `author`, `repository`, `homepage`, `bugs`, `main`, expanded `keywords`), and an explicit `files` array scoping the tarball to plugin content only. \`npm pack --dry-run\`: **41 files, 74.4 kB** — no project state, tests, or external vendored content leaks through.

## Install

### Claude Code
\`\`\`
/plugin marketplace add rizukirr/no-vibe
/plugin install no-vibe@no-vibe
\`\`\`

### Codex (new — marketplace install)
\`\`\`bash
codex plugin marketplace add rizukirr/no-vibe
codex plugin install no-vibe
\`\`\`

### Pi
\`\`\`bash
pi install git:github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe
\`\`\`

### Gemini CLI
\`\`\`bash
gemini extensions install https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe --ref=v2.0.3
\`\`\`

### OpenCode
Add to \`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json\`:
\`\`\`json
{
  \"\$schema\": \"https://opencode.ai/config.json\",
  \"plugin\": [\"no-vibe@git+https://github.com/rizukirr/no-vibe.git\"]
}
\`\`\`
Then fetch the command files (see \`INSTALL.opencode.md\`).

## Changes since v2.0.2

### Distribution & packaging
- \`3087dd2\` **test(codex):** new \`tests/test_codex_plugin.mjs\` parity test (manifest fields, version parity with \`package.json\`, hook script existence + executable bit, write/bash matcher coverage for both Claude and Codex tool names, author URL regression guard). \`test_validate_memory_write\` also wired into CI (was running locally but never in CI). \`workflow_dispatch\` added for manual triggering.
- \`c7e6008\` **fix(consistency):** unbroke the README platform-support table (footnote was splitting it; one row was orphaned below the footnote). Corrected a pre-existing \`author.github\` typo (\`rizkirr\` → \`rizukirr\`) in both \`.claude-plugin/plugin.json\` and \`.codex-plugin/plugin.json\`.
- \`d96d4c0\` **chore(release):** version bumped to \`2.0.3\` across all six version-coupled manifests (\`package.json\`, \`.claude-plugin/plugin.json\`, \`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json\`, \`gemini-extension.json\`, \`.pi-plugin/plugin.json\`, \`.codex-plugin/plugin.json\`).
- \`e798297\` **feat(distribution):** new \`.codex-plugin/plugin.json\` Codex marketplace manifest; promote native install commands per CLI in the README; \`gemini extensions install\` promoted as the recommended Gemini path; \`LICENSE\` (MIT) added; \`package.json\` filled out for npm publish.
